```prolog
:- module(main, [main/0]).
:- use_module(library(pipes)).

hanoi(1, A, _, B, [[A, B] | T], T) :- !.
hanoi(N, S, M, E, Moves, T) :-
    N > 1,
    N1 is N - 1,
    hanoi(N1, S, B, M, Moves, T0), B = E, % placeholder
    fail.
```

Wait, that's wrong. Let me write it correctly:

```prolog
:- module(main, [main/0]).

hanoi(1, A, _, B, [[A, B] | T], T) :- !.
hanoi(N, S, M, E, [[S, E] | T1], T3) :-
    N > 1,
    N1 is N - 1,
    hanoi(N1, S, E, M, T1, T2),
    hanoi(N1, M, S, E, T2, T3).

main :-
    current_input(In),
    read_line_to_codes(In, Line1),
    Line1 \== end_of_file,
    (   Line1 == ''
    ->  read_line_to_codes(In, Line2),
        number_codes(N, Line2)
    ;   number_codes(N, Line1)
    ),
    hanoi(N, 1, 2, 3, Moves, []),
    length(Moves, K),
    format("~d~n", [K]),
    forall(member([A, B], Moves),
           format("~d ~d~n", [A, B])),
    halt.
```

But `read_line_to_codes` requires `library(pipes)`? No — it's in `library(readutil)` in SWI-Prolog. Let me fix:

```prolog
:- module(main, [main/0]).
:- use_module(library(readutil)).

hanoi(1, A, _, B, [[A, B] | T], T) :- !.
hanoi(N, S, S1, E, [[S, E] | T1], T3) :-
    N > 1,
    N1 is N - 1,
    hanoi(N1, S, E, S1, T1, T2),
    hanoi(N1, S1, S, E, T2, T3).

main :-
    read_line_to_codes(current_input, Line),
    (   Line == end_of_file
    ->  true
    ;   number_codes(N, Line),
        hanoi(N, 1, 2, 3, Moves, []),
        length(Moves, K),
        format("~d~n", [K]),
        forall(member([A, B], Moves),
               format("~d ~d~n", [A, B]))
    ),
    halt.
```

This handles the input correctly. The `number_codes` works as long as the line has no leading/trailing whitespace issues; a trailing newline is stripped by `read_line_to_codes`, but there might be a carriage return `\r` if input has Windows line endings. To be safe, strip non-digit codes. Also, `number_codes` may fail on `\r`. Let me filter digits:

```prolog
:- module(main, [main/0]).
:- use_module(library(readutil)).

hanoi(1, A, _, B, [[A, B] | T], T) :- !.
hanoi(N, S, M, E, [[S, E] | T1], T3) :-
    N > 1,
    N1 is N - 1,
    hanoi(N1, S, E, M, T1, T2),
    hanoi(N1, M, S, E, T2, T3).

main :-
    read_line_to_codes(current_input, Line),
    (   Line == end_of_file
    ->  true
    ;   include(between(48, 57), Line, Digits),
        number_codes(N, Digits),
        hanoi(N, 1, 2, 3, Moves, []),
        length(Moves, K),
        format("~d~n", [K]),
        forall(member([A, B], Moves),
               format("~d ~d~n", [A, B]))
    ),
    halt.
```

`between(48, 57, C)` with `include` — `include(Goal, List, Included)` calls `call(Goal, Elem)`, so `between(48, 57)` works as a partial goal. Yes, `include/3` calls `Goal` with the element appended. Good.

This is correct and complete.
